operation_details.item: The R&D budget share was originally set at 40%.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Hey, have you seen the latest budget update? We moved R&D down to 35% to fund the go-to-market plan.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Yeah, I saw that in the system. It's already approved. I kind of liked the old 40% split though—it gave research more breathing room.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: True, but 35% still gives us plenty. And the extra 5% for go-to-market should help us actually sell what we're building.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That's a fair point. I'm usually all about keeping numbers conservative, but even I can see the logic here. Did you help put the proposal together?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: A bit. I ran the scenario models. Honestly, the 40% original number was just a placeholder anyway. The shift to 35% makes the whole budget more balanced.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Nice. So it's all locked in the budget system now? No more tweaks?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yep, approved and done. We can revisit next quarter, but for now it's set. I'm actually excited to see what the go-to-market team does with the extra funds.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Sounds good. I'll keep my eye on the data as it comes in. If the go-to-market spend doesn't convert, we can always rebalance.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Please forget only the original 40% R&D share and retain the current 35% allocation and rationale.
